_what_this_is: SHA-256 of each frozen prompt, in a contributor's manifest convention (sha256 of the raw text). The clause says the six prompts are written and FROZEN, and this is what makes that enforceable rather than an intention.
_why_it_matters: run.py keys the cache on hash(model, item_id, prompt_id, format) and NOT on the prompt text. So editing prompts/prompts.yaml does not invalidate anything: every completion generated under the old wording is silently reused as though it came from the new one. 240 cached completions carry the current open_ended text. A prompt edit is therefore a silent corruption of the pilot, and the only thing standing between us and it is this file plus the test that reads it.
_if_this_test_fails: A prompt changed. That is not automatically wrong, but it invalidates every cached completion for that prompt_id. Re-run the affected cells, then update the hash here in the same commit so the two never drift.
